title: Verb + preposition 4: of/for/from/on
subtitle: accuse of, pay for, suffer from, depend on
summary: Use the right preposition (of, for, from or on) after common verbs such as accuse, pay, apologise, blame, suffer and depend.

lesson.heading: Verb + of
lesson.text: These verbs take **of**: **accuse / suspect somebody of** something, **approve / disapprove of** something, **die of** (or **die from**) an illness, and **consist of** (= be made up of).

examples.text: Some students were **suspected of** cheating in the exam.
His parents don't **approve of** what he does, but they can't stop him.
We had an enormous meal. It **consisted of** seven courses.

lesson.heading: Verb + for
lesson.text: These verbs take **for**: **pay (somebody) for** something, **thank / forgive somebody for** something, **apologise (to somebody) for** something, and **blame somebody for** something. You can also say somebody **is to blame for** something.

examples.text: We didn't have enough money to **pay for** the meal.
I'll never **forgive them for** what they did.
When I realised I was wrong, I **apologised (to them) for** my mistake.
Everybody said that I **was to blame for** the accident.

left.label: pay FOR a thing, but pay a bill (no preposition)
left.text: We say pay a bill / a fine / a fee / tax / rent / a sum of money without a preposition.
examples: We didn't have enough money to **pay for** the meal.
We didn't have enough money to **pay the rent**.

right.label: blame somebody FOR, but blame a problem ON somebody
right.text: The preposition changes with the object.
examples: It wasn't my fault. Don't **blame it on** me.

lesson.heading: Verb + from
lesson.text: **suffer from** an illness etc. and **protect somebody / something from** something.

examples.text: There's been an increase in the number of people **suffering from** heart disease.
Sun cream **protects** the skin **from** the sun.

lesson.heading: Verb + on
lesson.text: **depend on**, **rely on**, **live on** money or food, and **congratulate / compliment somebody on** something. After **depend** you can use when / where / how etc. with or without **on**.

examples.text: I don't know what time we'll arrive. It **depends on** the traffic.
You can **rely on** Anna. She always keeps her promises.
'Are you going to buy it?' 'It **depends how** much it is.' or 'It **depends on how** much ...'
Michael's salary is very low. It isn't enough to **live on**.
I **congratulated her on** doing so well in her exams.
The meal was really good. I **complimented Mark on** his cooking skills.

lesson.heading: Summary
rows: accuse, suspect, approve, disapprove, die, consist
pay, thank, forgive, apologise, blame somebody ... for
depend, rely, live, congratulate, compliment, blame a problem ... on

lesson.text: You **pay for** a thing you buy (pay for the meal, pay for the tickets), but you **pay** a bill, a fine, a fee, rent or a sum of money with no preposition at all.

exercises.prompt: Are you going to apologise ___ what you did?
The apartment ___ three rooms, a kitchen and bathroom.
exercises.explanation: consist of = be made up of.

exercises.prompt: We finished our meal, paid ___ the bill, and left the restaurant.
exercises.explanation: We pay a bill / a fine / rent etc. with no preposition. We pay FOR a thing we buy.

exercises.prompt: The accident was my fault, so I had to ___ the repairs.
exercises.explanation: pay for something you buy or receive (the repairs).

exercises.prompt: Which preposition completes each sentence: of, for or on?

items.text: I was accused ___ lying, but I was telling the truth.
I called Helen to thank her ___ the present.
When something goes wrong, you always blame it ___ other people.
Most people approve ___ the government's policies.
Forgive me ___ interrupting, but I'd like to ask you something.
You know you can always rely ___ me if you need any help.
Do you blame the government ___ our economic problems?
My usual breakfast consists ___ fruit, cereal and coffee.

exercises.prompt: Jane won the tournament, so you congratulated her. Put the words in order.
exercises.answer: I congratulated her on winning the tournament.

exercises.prompt: Sandra eats only bread and eggs. In other words, Sandra lives ___.
exercises.explanation: live ON food or money = have only that to live on.

exercises.statement: Some people are dying from hunger, while others eat too much.
exercises.explanation: Correct. You can say die of or die from - both are possible.

exercises.statement: Sophie will have to borrow money to pay for her college fees.
exercises.explanation: Sophie will have to borrow money to pay her college fees. We pay a fee / a bill / a fine with no preposition.

exercises.prompt: Alex ___ back pain. He spends too much time working at his desk.
exercises.explanation: suffer FROM an illness or a pain.

exercises.prompt: Match the beginning of each sentence with its ending.

pairs.left: I called Jack to congratulate him
You were rude to Lisa. I think you should apologise
Anna doesn't have a job. She depends
We hope to go to the beach tomorrow, but it depends

exercises.statement: I don't know whether I'll go out tonight. It depends how I feel.
exercises.explanation: Correct. After depend you can use how / when / where etc. with or without on: It depends how I feel or It depends on how I feel.
